prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S935: The system records the affected function, the detected condition, and the time of transition so that operators can assess the scope and duration of the impairment.
S936: Safety functions take priority over energy production, maintenance throughput, and schedule recovery in every degraded mode.
S937: Turbine Controller retains protective control locally when the supervisory connection is unavailable, while the Shore Control Room monitors the loss of visibility.
S938: If remote commands cannot be confirmed, the Control Engineer suspends those commands and uses approved local procedures until reliable control is restored.
S939: The Weather Service and Weather Analyst support entry into Weather Hold when forecast or observed conditions exceed approved operating limits.
S940: A turbine with a safety-critical fault is placed in Turbine Lockout until the fault is assessed and the required work is authorized.
S941: The Offshore Substation enters Substation Degraded when a protection, auxiliary supply, or monitoring impairment limits safe switching or export capability.
S942: The Grid Interface Relay applies the configured response to a Grid Constraint, and the Grid Dispatcher is advised when generation capability changes.
S943: Marine activity is reduced or suspended in Vessel Standby when weather, visibility, communications, or vessel capability is insufficient for safe transfer.
S944: The Marine Coordinator and Vessel Master confirm that personnel and vessels can remain safely accounted for during an extended interruption.
S945: The Fire Detection Panel and Emergency Generator remain essential services during degraded operation and are not bypassed to recover production.
S946: The SCADA Gateway preserves available status and alarm information, while the SCADA Engineer investigates missing or inconsistent indications.
S947: The Fleet Dispatch Console presents operational restrictions so that the Duty Planner can prioritize urgent safety work and maintainable generation capacity.
S948: The Maintenance Planning Engine separates safety-critical work from tasks that can safely wait until normal access and support are available.
S949: The HSE Officer reviews any proposed workaround that changes established access, isolation, or personnel-control arrangements.
S950: A degraded condition is escalated when its duration, uncertainty, or effect on adjacent equipment increases beyond the approved operating envelope.
S951: The Control Engineer coordinates technical recovery with the relevant field and shore roles before any protection or operating restriction is removed.
S952: Recovery begins only after the initiating condition has been corrected or bounded and the responsible operator has confirmed that the equipment is stable.
S953: Required inspections and functional checks are completed before affected equipment is returned to automatic control or normal duty.
